title: Emit one absolute self-referencing canonical per indexable page
statement: Each indexable page declares exactly one canonical link whose href is an absolute URL on the production origin and equals the URL that serves the page, with no second canonical element anywhere in the document.
rationale: A single unambiguous self-reference tells the engine which address represents this content; a missing declaration leaves the choice to heuristics, and two competing declarations are treated as a conflict the engine resolves on its own.
implementation: Derive the value from the resolved route path joined to the configured production origin, emitted once from the layer that owns the document head. Remove any duplicate canonical contributed by a plugin, layout, or CMS field before adding a new one.

verification.method: Count canonical link elements in the served response for a route sample and record each href alongside the request URL that produced it.

title: Point every canonical at a URL that returns 200 and stays indexable
statement: The target of every canonical declaration responds 200 without redirecting, and that target does not itself carry a noindex directive or a robots.txt rule that blocks it.
rationale: A canonical aimed at a redirect, an error, or a page excluded from indexing asks the engine to consolidate signals onto an address that cannot be indexed, so the declaration is discarded and the consolidation never happens.
implementation: Collect the distinct canonical targets across the route inventory and request each one, then reconcile any target that redirects by pointing the canonical at the redirect destination instead. Where the target is deliberately excluded from indexing, the canonical is the thing to change, not the exclusion.

verification.method: Request each distinct canonical target and record its status code, redirect chain, and robots directives together.

title: Strip tracking and session parameters from canonical values
statement: A canonical href contains no campaign, referral, session, or affiliate parameter, even when the request that produced the page carried one.
rationale: Echoing the inbound query string into the canonical turns every shared link into its own canonical address, which defeats the consolidation the declaration exists to perform.
implementation: Build the canonical from the route's own path and its content-defining parameters only, using an allowlist of parameters that change what the page shows. Never construct the value by copying the incoming request URL.

verification.method: Request a page with campaign and session parameters appended, then confirm the emitted canonical omits them.

title: Consolidate duplicate route aliases onto one canonical URL
statement: Where several routes serve the same primary content - a legacy path, a short link, a category-scoped variant - all of them declare the same canonical target rather than each declaring itself.
rationale: Aliases that self-canonicalize present the same content as several independent pages, so external links and internal signals are divided among copies instead of accumulating on the address the site wants ranked.
implementation: Identify alias groups by comparing the primary content each route renders, not by comparing paths. For each group choose one address, have the aliases canonicalize to it, and prefer a permanent redirect over a canonical wherever the alias exists only for history.

verification.method: Fetch every route in an identified alias group and confirm they all declare the same canonical href.

title: Link internally to the canonical form of each destination
statement: Internal anchor hrefs resolve to the canonical address of their destination, so navigation does not route readers and crawlers through aliases, tracking variants, or redirects.
rationale: Internal links are a signal about which address the site itself treats as authoritative, and pointing them at non-canonical variants contradicts the canonical declaration while adding a redirect hop to every traversal.
implementation: Generate internal hrefs from the same URL builder that produces canonical values, so one change updates both. Where links come from authored content, resolve them at build or render time instead of trusting the stored string.

verification.method: Extract same-origin anchor hrefs from the served pages and compare each resolved target against that target's own canonical declaration.

title: List only canonical URLs in the sitemap
statement: Every entry in a sitemap is an address that declares itself canonical; alias URLs, redirecting URLs, and parameter variants do not appear as entries.
rationale: A sitemap is a statement about which addresses the site wants processed, so listing a non-canonical variant contradicts the canonical declaration and spends the crawl the submission requested on a URL that will be discarded.
implementation: Generate sitemap entries from the same route inventory and URL builder the canonical uses, filtering out anything the inventory marks as an alias or a redirect source. Regenerate rather than hand-editing entries.

verification.method: For each sitemap entry, request the URL and confirm the canonical it declares is the entry URL itself.

title: Self-canonicalize each paginated page rather than the series entry point
statement: Page two and beyond of a paginated sequence declare their own address as canonical, not the address of the first page in the sequence.
rationale: Canonicalizing a sequence onto its first page tells the engine the later pages are duplicates of it, so the items that appear only on those pages are dropped from consideration along with the URLs that hold them.
implementation: Include the page parameter or path segment in the canonical value for every page after the first. If the intent is instead to expose the whole set at one address, build a view-all page and canonicalize the sequence to that, not to page one.

verification.method: Fetch at least the second and third page of a paginated sequence and confirm each declared canonical carries its own page identifier.

title: Declare canonicals for non-HTML documents with an HTTP Link header
statement: A PDF or other non-HTML resource that is reachable at more than one address carries its canonical declaration in a Link response header, because the format has no document head to hold a link element.
rationale: Without a header there is no place to express canonicalization for these resources, so duplicate copies of the same document at different addresses stay independent and compete with each other.
implementation: Add the header at the layer that serves the file - object storage metadata, CDN response rules, or the download route handler - using the rel=canonical link relation with an absolute URL. Verify the header survives the CDN, which may strip unknown headers.

verification.method: Request the document URL and read the Link response header, confirming it carries a rel=canonical parameter with an absolute target.

title: Build canonical URLs from configuration rather than the request Host header
statement: The origin used in canonical values comes from deployment configuration or a validated host allowlist, never from the unvalidated Host or X-Forwarded-Host header of the incoming request.
rationale: A canonical assembled from an attacker-supplied header lets any host that reaches the application inject its own address into the page's canonical declaration, which turns a header injection into a canonicalization change on real pages.
implementation: Read the origin from an environment variable or config module at startup. If the deployment genuinely serves several hosts, validate the incoming host against an explicit allowlist and fall back to the primary origin when it does not match.

verification.method: Send a request carrying a Host header for an unrelated domain and confirm the emitted canonical still names the configured origin.
